app.title: Remote-sensing change detection platform (two-date spectral-index change detection, with land-cover classification and pixel trend pages)
app.summary: The person picks a study area, either from a boundary file or by searching a place name. They set two years, a seasonal month window, a satellite source and a spectral index. The interface then fetches the matching cloud-masked imagery in the background, or reuses a cached copy. Next the person sets the change thresholds, the minimum patch size and the sampling limits, and runs the detection. This computes the index difference between the two dates, grades every pixel into severe or moderate loss, stable, or moderate or strong gain, and drops patches that are too small. They get a graded change map they can click to read a pixel's class, a table and charts of area per change class, and one sample point per change patch. The map, the points (GeoJSON and CSV) and PNG and PDF reports can all be downloaded.

task.text: Find and measure where a surface index changed between two image dates over an area, and produce graded change maps, area totals and points to check on the ground.

data.text: Multispectral satellite raster bands for one area at two dates, clipped to a boundary polygon. They become a per-pixel index difference, a graded change raster, per-class area statistics and a set of sample points with coordinates.
data.item: a pixel of the area-of-interest grid, grouped into connected change patches

stage.text: detecting and measuring land-surface change between two image dates, before checking it on the ground

mechanism.text: A sidebar holds the area, period, source, index and threshold settings that drive a tabbed workspace: get imagery, run, result map, statistics, sample points. Each tab unlocks once the step before it has finished in the background, and the result map, class-area table and point table all read from the same graded raster.

field.text: bi-temporal change detection on spectral indices in satellite remote sensing

workflow.name: compare a measured surface at two dates and grade where it changed

steps.here: Choose a boundary GeoJSON or fetch one by place-name search, set two years, a month window, a data source and an index, then press 'collect imagery'. A background job searches the catalogue, downloads the bands and masks clouds, or reports a matching local cache.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Set the mode (multi-level, binary or random forest), the change and severe thresholds, the minimum patch area and bilateral pre-filtering, then run. The job differences the index between the two dates, grades pixels into five classes and filters out small connected patches, with step-by-step progress shown.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A web map lays the graded change layer over the boundary, with an opacity slider, a legend and a choice of street or satellite basemap.
Clicking the map converts the location to a pixel and reports its change class, coordinates and row and column.
A table gives area in hectares and share per change class plus the changed total, with bar and pie charts and a side-by-side view of the graded map and highlighted change.
Each change patch gives one interior point, kept largest first under an optional count limit and minimum spacing in metres, and listed with lon/lat, area and class.
Download buttons save the Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) change raster, sample points as GeoJSON and CSV, the report PNG and an automatic PDF report.

distinctive: Seven spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, MNDWI, NBR, EVI, SAVI, NDBI), each with its own class names, colours and default thresholds. The thresholds can instead be estimated from the robust noise of stable pixels.
The minimum patch area is set in square metres and converted to pixels using the real pixel size of the analysis grid. Each change class is filtered separately.
The sample points are guaranteed to fall inside their patch even for concave or ring-shaped patches, and are thinned by distance in projected metres.
Imagery for one date is cached under area, source, year, months, cloud cap and band set, so other pages and later runs reuse it without downloading again.

Sister pages use the same imagery: one classifies land cover with GMM clusters mapped to classes plus an active-learning queue of uncertain patches, and one runs per-pixel Mann-Kendall trend tests with Theil-Sen slopes over many years.

parts.summary: Lays the graded change classes over the boundary on a web map with opacity, basemap switching and a legend. Clicking a spot reports that pixel's change class, and download buttons sit below for the result files.
